verdict.rationale: DBOS ships an official MCP server (dbos-mcp) that lets an LLM/agent 'analyze and manage your DBOS workflows,' and a runtime probe confirms it completes a full keyless MCP handshake, giving AI agents a natural-language-driven interface to inspect/manage workflows via Conductor. However, this is scoped to workflow observability/management (pause, restart, fork) rather than full natural-language operation of the whole product (e.g., defining or writing workflows), and the primary interfaces remain code annotations and a traditional CLI (dbosctl). Missing for 10: broader NL coverage beyond workflow ops (e.g., authoring/config via NL), independent user reports of using the MCP server for NL control, and NL support outside Conductor's scope.
